turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Yes, Miss Havisham. I'll call Estella.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Let the boy be. I shall speak with Estella.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I'll stay here then, Miss Havisham. Should I do anything else for you?

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: I shall call her myself. You may wait here, Pip. Let the clocks stand still.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I will wait here, Miss Havisham. Is there anything else I can do while I am here?

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: I have no need for your assistance at this moment, Pip. Observe and learn from the world around you.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I will do that, Miss Havisham. I will just wait here and observe.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: You will notice that time has little meaning here, Pip. The clocks remain frozen as a testament to my own halted life.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I see that, Miss Havisham. The clocks are indeed still, like the rest of the room.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: I have no desire to move forward. My life is a still tableau, preserved in amber.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I understand, Miss Havisham. It must be very strange to live like this.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Observe, Pip. See how the world outside has moved on, while I remain ensnared in this moment of betrayal and heartache.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Yes, Miss Havisham. It looks as if everything here is trapped in time, just like you.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: And so it shall remain, Pip. You see, I have no intention of letting go of this pain. It is my prison and my sanctuary.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I see, Miss Havisham. Your home feels like a place from a long time ago, even though it is still very much here.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Estella, fetch some wine for our guest and myself. Let him taste the bitterness that clings to these walls.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Yes, Miss Havisham. I will sit here quietly while Estella fetches the wine.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: You see, Pip, time has no meaning here. The clocks may stand still, but my heart does not.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Yes, Miss Havisham. I understand that time seems different here, like everything is paused.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: And so it shall remain, Pip. My heart is a clock that ticks on, no matter how the world outside moves.

opening.speaker: Pip
opening.text: Mr. Pumblechook’s boy, ma’am. Come—to play.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Come nearer; let me look at you. Come close.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Look at me. You are not afraid of a woman who has never seen the sun since you were born?

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Do you know what I touch here?

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: I am tired. I want diversion, and I have done with men and women. Play.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: I sometimes have sick fancies, and I have a sick fancy that I want to see some play. There, there! with an impatient movement of the fingers of her right hand; play, play, play!

opening.speaker: Pip
opening.text: No, ma’am, I am very sorry for you, and very sorry I can’t play just now. If you complain of me I shall get into trouble with my sister, so I would do it if I could; but it’s so new here, and so strange, and so fine,—and melancholy—.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: So new to him, so old to me; so strange to him, so familiar to me; so melancholy to both of us! Call Estella.
